quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: Stop, just like a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not need to stop completely.
Road conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, just like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely, just like a stop sign. Come to a full stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes ahead.
A divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
An intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving both ways ahead.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The driver who honks first.
The car driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control signs, you must yield to a car coming from your right.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a busy intersection but cannot see all the lanes. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and go when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for another driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane as traffic clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes are clear and safe to cross.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Find a different route.
Drive normally.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car will need more time to stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Get back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bike lanes and a cyclist is ahead. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must move.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, wait for oncoming traffic to clear, then pass with plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any vehicle, but give extra space—at least 3 feet on regular roads or 5 feet on faster roads. Do not honk unless necessary, as it may startle the rider.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Let other drivers know what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Only drive on side streets.
Avoid driving during busy times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Signal when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your horn or emergency lights when needed to alert others.

questions.question: You are in an accident and someone is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move them unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless they are in danger. Moving them incorrectly can make injuries worse. Keep them warm while waiting for help. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: You may pass if it is safe.
Both directions travel in the same direction.
You cannot pass.
You may pass, even if it is dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A single dashed yellow line separates traffic going in opposite directions. You may pass if it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What do two solid yellow lines on the road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is not allowed.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during the day only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mean traffic on the other side is moving in the opposite direction. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass, from either direction.

questions.question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?

options.text: New drivers
Human error
Bad weather
Bad roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers don't see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Talk to other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: What does an arrow painted on the road mean?

options.text: You may make the movement shown by the arrow if you choose to.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow only if traffic lights are broken.
You must stop completely before making the movement shown by the arrow.
You must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must make the movement shown by the arrow while obeying traffic signals.
questions.explanation: An arrow on the road tells drivers in that lane they must move in the direction shown. Follow all traffic signs and signals before moving in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: When riding in a vehicle, small children:

options.text: Can be safely held by an adult.
Will be safe standing on the floor in the back.
Will not get hurt in a crash because they are small.
Must never stand in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must never stand in the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Use special child seats for small children. No adult is strong enough to hold a child during a crash or sudden stop. Always use a proper seat to keep children safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Low clearance.
Merging traffic.
Prepare to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare you for hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may enter from a side road.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle share half a lane with you.
Pass the motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full-size vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give it a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room to share, the motorcycle needs space to move safely.

questions.question: What color are most warning signs?

options.text: Red
Yellow
Green
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. They warn drivers about unexpected road conditions.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs
Pedestrians
Other vehicles
Street lights

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:

options.text: Vehicles in the roundabout
Bicyclists in the roundabout
Pedestrians in the roundabout
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in it.

questions.question: Lanes moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with a single rider.
A car driver must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
Other drivers can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when it slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car driver must move completely into the left lane to pass a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Make sure your entire car is in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: When may you use your horn?

options.text: When you have to stop quickly.
When you are passing another car.
When you have lost control of your car.
When you are passing a bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you have lost control of your car.
questions.explanation: Use your horn if you lose control of your vehicle. This alerts other drivers to the danger.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal to slow down before applying the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas pedal first, then apply steady brake pressure. This turns on your brake lights and stops the vehicle smoothly.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: The driver.
Passengers on long drives.
Everyone on an expressway.
Everyone in the car every time it is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time it is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your car should wear a seat belt on every trip. Without a seat belt, a person becomes a dangerous projectile in a crash.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the road edge. What should you do?

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the road.
Speed up and steer back onto the road gradually.
Slam on the brakes and stop.
Gently use the brakes to slow down and turn back onto the road at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently use the brakes to slow down and turn back onto the road at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep your wheels off the road and slow down by gently applying the brakes. Once at a safe speed, turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not sharply jerk the steering wheel.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers that a school zone is coming. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign tells drivers that right turns are not allowed. Drivers must obey this sign.

questions.question: At night, when should you dim your headlights for an oncoming car?

options.text: When the other car is within 500 feet.
When the other car is within 400 feet.
When the other car is within 450 feet.
When the other car is within 350 feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the other car is within 500 feet.
questions.explanation: Switch to low beam headlights when an oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet away.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to follow instructions are called:

options.text: Regulatory signs.
Warning signs.
Information signs.
Guide signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs require drivers to obey instructions. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: Merging traffic
Proceed with caution.
Pedestrian crossing
Come to a full stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means you should drive carefully and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: Drivers under 18 cannot text or talk on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when talking on a cell phone while driving.
Drivers 18 and older cannot text while driving.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, drivers under 18 cannot talk or text on a cell phone while driving. Drivers 18 and older must use a hands-free device when using a cell phone.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance becomes poor.
You are less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, makes it hard to see clearly, damages your judgment of speed and distance, makes it harder to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
A circular intersection is ahead.
Traffic in this lane must turn in the direction of the arrow.
Lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with multiple passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that parking spaces are reserved for people with disabled parking permits.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while having a conversation while driving.
Only watches the vehicle directly in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for items in your vehicle, read, look at scenery, or daydream while driving. Always scan the road, check your mirrors, and look at your dashboard regularly. These habits will keep you focused on driving.
